To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new computer level is required to support the social aspects of collaborative problem solving.
A knowledge level for collaboration is needed in order to support multi-agent problem solving.
(a) a new computer level, called the cooperation knowledge, level has been defined and (b) a domain independent model of joint responsibility for multi-agent problem solving has been developed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing models of social behaviour which are sufficiently rich to support the design of intelligent multi-agent problem solving systems.
the design of multi-agent systems which are able to cooperate in order to tackle problems that they cannot solve individually.
the development of a new level of knowledge for problem solving systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
joint responsibility is an effective model for collaborative problem solving.
the joint responsibility model provides a principled and practical way for agents to work together to solve a common problem.
this paper provides a model of social interaction which is both domain independent and applicable to a wide variety of real-world domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the knowledge level is not a static, fixed level of description, but rather a dynamic, evolving one.
the cooperation knowledge level is an appropriate level for describing and developing models of multi-agent problem solving in dynamic, unpredictable environments.
we have developed a new level of computer science which is based on a new way of looking at the social aspects of problem solving.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a knowledge level approach to multi-agent problem solving is a useful tool for understanding the nature of the problem, the nature of the solution and for developing the solution itself.
the knowledge level provides a natural and intuitive framework for developing models of social interaction.
a new level of computer science is required to support the design and implementation of collaborative multi-agent systems.
